purpose: Pinned external-reference distance gates for first-party OfficeIMO Office-to-PDF converters. These budgets measure improvement against Microsoft Office output; they do not claim pixel equivalence.

sanitization.source: Synthetic delivery-summary report
sanitization.replacements: Machine, customer, analyst, and domain identifiers were replaced with example values before export.

sanitization.source: Repository-authored synthetic DOCX control exported independently by desktop Microsoft Word
sanitization.replacements: Creator and last modifier use OfficeIMO synthetic controls; personal company and manager metadata removed.

scenarios.qualification: Same DOCX exported by native Word and OfficeIMO; complete page comparison plus focused geometry/format regression tests. Finite control, not a universal fidelity claim. Raster budgets include observed Windows system fonts and Linux font substitution; glyph sizing and picture geometry have separate regression assertions.

scenarios.qualification: Column/paragraph anchored picture and right-tab title with explicit paragraph defaults. Source validated with Open XML SDK 3.5.1 before read-only native export; same input hash retained. Native output qualifies finite visual layout; editable PDF field semantics have separate regression assertions.
scenarios.calibrationNotes: Windows Poppler 26.07.0 and WSL Linux Poppler 24.02.0 at 72 dpi. Each platform compares the native reference and candidate with its own rasterizer. Linux substitutes Liberation Sans for the unavailable Arial and Calibri source families. Page counts match on both platforms. Candidate picture pages of 400 by 500 pixels are padded to the native reference size of 400 by 501 pixels on opaque white.

scenarios.qualification: Same schema-valid standalone synthetic DOCX exported read-only by native Word and the first-party converter. Complete-page raster distance measures this finite control; focused field, glyph and geometry regressions cover their own contracts. Initial appearance preserves cached formatting and surrounding text; filled-field behavior is qualified separately.
scenarios.calibrationNotes: Poppler 26.07.0 on Windows and Poppler 24.02.0 on WSL Linux, at 72 dpi. Both platforms preserve the expected one-page content and field structure with no rasterizer syntax or resource diagnostics. Raster budgets use the largest measured platform distance with the existing 20 percent plus fixed-headroom convention. Windows embeds the source Arial faces; Linux substitutes Liberation Sans.

scenarios.knownLimitations: Automatic line spacing in this ordinary mixed Latin/East Asian font sample retains a measured difference from Word in natural line height and following-text placement, even when source fonts are available and glyphs share a baseline. This is independent of the content-control wrapper. The raster distance alone does not establish glyph or filled-state equivalence.
